title: On one GOES scale (1976-2026), Cycle 25 has no flare excess above 1.3x Cycles 21-23 per F10.7, sunspot number or Mg II; sunspot number fell 24% against F10.7 and Mg II, with a 14% step in 1981
abstract: Question: on one GOES flux scale and over five solar cycles, which activity index gives cycle-independent M-flare rates, is Cycle 25 unusual, and which index changed when the F10.7-sunspot relation changed? Method: we joined the NOAA GOES X-ray event reports (1975-1998) and the SWPC list of an earlier publication (1998-2026) on the old GOES-1..15 operational scale (Cycles 21-25; 8,171 flares of M1 or more). We fitted Poisson spline models of daily flare counts against F10.7, the SILSO sunspot number (SN) or the Mg II index, with one factor per cycle and 27-day block-bootstrap intervals. We compared SN, F10.7, Mg II and USAF/NOAA and SWPC sunspot areas and numbers with each other, with phase-matched placebo windows and a change-point scan, and we matched the event reports to archived GOES-3, -5 and -6 fluxes. Results: with full cycles, the cycle factors of the flare rate agree within the block-bootstrap noise for all indices and thresholds; with cycles limited to their first 83 months, about 15% of real spread remains for F10.7 and SN. Relative to the mean of Cycles 21-23, Cycle 25 is 0.54-1.28 times for all indices and thresholds; the largest value is 1.28 for M1 flares per SN, and at M5 per SN it is 1.06. SN at matched F10.7 is 1.19, 1.16, 1.06, 1.00 and 0.91 times the Cycle 24 value for Cycles 21-25, and at matched Mg II 1.27, 1.35, 1.22, 1.00 and 0.93, while F10.7 at matched Mg II stays at 0.99-1.07. SWPC sunspot numbers and areas show the same Cycle 24-25 decline. In January 1981, when sunspot-number production moved from Zurich to Brussels, SN falls by 14% relative to F10.7 and by 15% relative to Mg II, but F10.7 relative to Mg II does not change; thus the Mg II data do not support the earlier explanation of this step as an F10.7 change. Flare rates at matched activity are 1.0-2.0 times higher after the cycle maximum. A 1.7-2.3 times step of the flare rate in late 1980 coincides with a gap in the archived XRS data of the report satellite. Limitations: five cycles with Cycle 25 incomplete, possible GOES-2 scale differences in 1980-1983, Mg II composite source changes, and placebo SN excursions of up to 24%.

citations.reason: We reuse its SWPC event list with true-scale peaks, its GOES-8..15 science/operational ratio, and its SWPC sunspot data, and we extend its comparison to five cycles.
We use the same NOAA GOES X-ray report files (identical SHA-256) and its 2017 flux-scale check.
Clette (2021) attributes the 1981 F10.7-SN step to F10.7; our Mg II comparison does not support that attribution.
